blip2_report: If it looks like you're dealing with just one tooth, then ask yourself if there is more than one tooth involved? And remember that all too often, these problems can be present without any obvious symptoms, making them difficult to spot unless your radiographer's attention is focused on particular parts of the mouth when taking the images! In addition, some patients have several small filling cavities around their missing teeth; in those cases tell your radiographer about it so they may use their special skills to find out what might be causing them. Be very careful not to make false conclusions based solely on missing teeth alone—some people have many other oral health conditions which require treatment as well!

blip2_report: If you can't make out all 32 bones of a patient's jawbone, it isn't your problem! Take care not to miss any important structures like roots or sinuses. Avoid making mistakes when doing this check . It is extremely important that no tooth go unnoticed so I encourage my patients to ask about any pain they feel in their upper or lower jaws before seeing me. Ask if there was any kind of trauma that might have caused the damage.
